stories.title: Africa: 'Too Arrogant, Too Sure of Itself' France Confronts Its Legacy in Africa
stories.summary: Africa: 'Too Arrogant, Too Sure of Itself' France Confronts Its Legacy in Africa 23 October 2026 Radio France Internationale By Alison Hird Fifteen years after France promised a new relationship with Africa, Paris is still struggling to reconcile its rejection of colonial-era interference with its desire to retain influence on the continent. RFI Africa specialist Christophe Boisbouvier argues in a new book that France can still build a partnership of equals - based on respect rather than arrogance or domination. "Too arrogant, too sure of itself, France failed to see the anti-French wave coming," Boisbouvier says. His book, Françafrique Is Dead, Long Live Africa-France , examines the breakdown of France's old model of relations with the continent. For decades after African countries gained independence, Paris maintained privileged relationships with friendly leaders and sought to protect its strategic interests - sometimes through military intervention. The system, known as Françafrique , gradually became synonymous with a neo-colonial pattern of French influence and patronage.

stories.title: Africa: Wcaf V - African Development Bank Group and UK Export Finance Sign MOU to Mobilise Financing for Africa
stories.summary: Wcaf V - African Development Bank Group and UK Export Finance Sign MOU to Mobilise Financing for Africa 23 October 2026 Content from a Premium Partner African Development Bank (Abidjan) The African Development Bank Group (AfDB) and UK Export Finance (UKEF), the United Kingdom's export credit agency, have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen cooperation on co-financing projects across Africa and mobilise additional resources for the continent's sustainable development. Abdul Kamara, Officer in Charge, Vice President of the African Development Bank Group, and Tim Reid, Chief Executive of UK Export Finance, signed the agreement on 21 October in Conakry, Guinea, on the sidelines of the fifth UK-West and Central Francophone Africa Trade and Investment Forum (WCAF V). It is the first framework agreement between the two institutions. "Africa's financing needs call for partnerships that bring additional capital to the continent at scale. This agreement with UK Export Finance gives our cooperation a structured framework and opens new opportunities to finance the infrastructure and investments that will drive Africa's growth," said Abdul Kamara, OIC Vice President of the African Development Bank Group . The Memorandum of Understanding provides a framework for the two institutions to identify, assess and develop co-financing opportunities for sovereign and non-sovereign operations in the Bank's regional member countries, drawing on each institution's financial instruments.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe Urged to Rethink Social Protection Funding Amid Rising Needs
stories.summary: Zimbabwe Urged to Rethink Social Protection Funding Amid Rising Needs 23 October 2026 263Chat (Harare) By Elia Ntali Zimbabwe needs sustainable and inclusive financing models to protect vulnerable households from poverty, unemployment and climate-related shocks, Deputy Minister of Labour and Social Welfare Advocate Mercy Dinha has said. Speaking at the Social Protection Conference in Bulawayo, Advocate Dinha called for a shift in how the country mobilises and allocates resources for social assistance, warning that growing needs and limited public finances were putting pressure on existing support systems. She said social protection should be treated as an investment in national development rather than simply an expense incurred when people fall into hardship. "Social protection is not merely an intervention for people experiencing poverty. It is an essential instrument of social justice, economic stability, human capital development and national transformation," she said. stories.title: Kenya: High Court Suspends Joho's Directive Allowing Fishing in Lake Nakuru
stories.summary: Kenya: High Court Suspends Joho's Directive Allowing Fishing in Lake Nakuru 23 October 2026 Capital FM (Nairobi) By Correspondent Nakuru — The High Court in Nakuru has temporarily suspended a directive by Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs Cabinet Secretary Hassan Joho allowing fishermen to resume fishing in Lake Nakuru National Park. Justice Abdi Hassan issued the orders after the Consumer Federation of Kenya (COFEK) moved to court, warning that fish harvested from the lake could contain dangerous levels of heavy metals and pose a risk to consumers. The court barred the Interior Cabinet Secretary, the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS), the Kenya Fisheries Service and the National Police Service from implementing or enforcing Joho's directive pending the hearing and determination of the case. The orders come a week after Joho issued the directive on October 16 during an economic empowerment forum hosted by Nakuru Governor Susan Kihika at the Agricultural Society of Kenya Showground in Nakuru. stories.title: West Africa: Qnet Reports Rescue of 300 Scam Victims, Strengthens Fight Against Fraud in West Africa
stories.summary: West Africa: Qnet Reports Rescue of 300 Scam Victims, Strengthens Fight Against Fraud in West Africa 23 October 2026 The Liberian Investigator (Monrovia) By Blamo N. Toe International direct-selling company QNET says its collaboration with law enforcement agencies across West Africa has helped rescue more than 300 suspected scam victims in Ghana, as the company intensifies efforts to combat fraudulent activities carried out by individuals misusing its name and products. The company also disclosed that it has referred 158 cases to authorities, assisted more than 3,000 victims in returning to their countries or families and terminated 141 independent distributor accounts for violating its policies. The disclosures were made during QNET VCON Malaysia 2026 media webinars held Oct. 22 for journalists in Liberia and Sierra Leone, focusing on the company's anti-fraud initiatives, law enforcement partnerships and efforts to protect the public from deceptive recruitment schemes. Speaking during the virtual engagement, QNET Regional General Manager for West and Central Africa Cherif Sarr said the company's cooperation with Ghana's Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has produced results in identifying suspected fraud networks and assisting victims.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Rejects Key Evidence in Dasuki's N33.2bn Trial
stories.summary: Nigeria: Court Rejects Key Evidence in Dasuki's N33.2bn Trial 23 October 2026 Premium Times (Abuja) By Falmata Daniel The judge ruled that the statements "failed to comply with sections 15(4) and 17(2) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act." The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) High Court in Maitama, Abuja, on Friday rejected key exhibits the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) presented to prove its N33.2billion fraud charges against former National Security Adviser (NSA) Sambo Dasuki and his co-defendant. The rejected exhibits were seven extra-judicial statements attributed to Mr Dasuki's co-defendant, Aminu Baba-Kusa. The EFCC took the statements when Mr Baba-Kusa was in its custody in 2015. Trial judge Charles Agbaza rejected the seven extra-judicial statements in a ruling it delivered after nearly eight months of a trial-within-trial that focussed on the admissibility of the statements. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines Mr Agbaza ruled that the statements "failed to comply with Sections 15(4) and 17(2) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act." It is unclear yet how crucial the rejected statements are to the prosecution's case.

stories.title: Paddy Donnelly obituary
stories.summary: Paddy Donnelly came to London from South Africa in the early 80s to work for the International Defence and Aid Fund for Southern Africa View image in fullscreen Paddy Donnelly came to London from South Africa in the early 80s to work for the International Defence and Aid Fund for Southern Africa Obituary Paddy Donnelly obituary My husband, Paddy Donnelly, who has died aged 70, was a South African who moved in the early 1980s to London. There he worked for the International Defence and Aid Fund for Southern Africa (IDAF), which funded the legal costs of people tried or imprisoned for anti-apartheid activity. In addition to its legal work, the IDAF had a large archive of photographs relating to apartheid, and Paddy ran that side of the operation, processing and distributing photos of ongoing state violence to media outlets, campaigning groups and many other organisations. He was an accomplished photographer himself, and many of his photos were held in the archive. He had begun by taking pictures of townships and displaced people’s camps, and when he came to the UK he photographed anti-apartheid political meetings as well as visiting or exiled South African singers, musicians and activists.

stories.title: Nigeria: Ebola - FG Orders Strict Screening At Nigeria's Entry Points
stories.summary: Nigeria: Ebola - FG Orders Strict Screening At Nigeria's Entry Points 23 October 2026 Premium Times (Abuja) By Fortune Eromonsele The Ministry of Health says the directive follows concerns raised by the Office of the National Security Adviser over reported breaches of approved Ebola entry protocols. The federal government has directed relevant agencies and health institutions to strictly enforce Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) screening and other entry protocols at Nigeria's designated points of entry following reports of non-compliance with approved measures. The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare announced the directive in a statement issued on Friday, following concerns raised by the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) over reported breaches of the government-approved protocols. The directive was contained in a circular dated 22 October and signed by the ministry's Permanent Secretary, Daju Kachollom, on behalf of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate. stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia's Abiy Inaugurates Major Megech Irrigation Dam
stories.summary: Ethiopia's Abiy Inaugurates Major Megech Irrigation Dam 23 October 2026 Horn Diplomat (Hargeisa) By Kadir Moustapha Gondar — Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on Friday inaugurated the Megech Irrigation Dam Project in Gondar, a major infrastructure development aimed at expanding agricultural production, improving water supplies and creating economic opportunities for surrounding communities. The dam, with a storage capacity of 185 million cubic metres, is expected to irrigate more than 17,000 hectares of farmland, directly benefiting tens of thousands of farmers, Abiy said in a statement posted on X. "Today, we officially inaugurated the Megech Irrigation Dam Project, a major milestone for historic Gondar and its surrounding community," Abiy said. The prime minister said the project had faced years of delays and implementation challenges before the government resolved obstacles to its completion through its Medemer development philosophy. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Beyond agricultural irrigation, the dam is expected to provide reliable drinking water to Gondar and nearby towns, supporting efforts to improve access to essential services. Abiy said the artificial lake created by the dam would also support fisheries, urban agriculture and tourism development, potentially generating employment opportunities for young people and stimulating economic activity in the region. "The artificial lake will foster urban agriculture, large-scale fisheries, and tourism resorts, creating massive job opportunities for local youth," he said.

stories.title: Kenya: Calls for Penalties Follow 12-Story Building Collapse
stories.summary: Kenya: Sakaja Seeks Tougher Penalties for Rogue Developers After Eastleigh Building Collapse Capitol FM A building under construction collapsed in the Eastleigh neighborhood of Nairobi. 23 October 2026 Capital FM (Nairobi) Nairobi — Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has called for tougher penalties against rogue developers and the restoration of prosecutorial powers to county governments following the collapse of an incomplete 12-storey building in Eastleigh. Sakaja said weak penalties for violating construction regulations undermine enforcement efforts and allow developers to compromise building safety, putting lives at risk. Speaking as he led multi-agency rescue operations at the site along 1st Avenue, 9th Street, the Governor urged professional bodies representing architects, engineers and quantity surveyors to take action against developers who dismiss qualified experts after obtaining construction approvals. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines He said some developers engage licensed professionals to secure approvals but subsequently remove them from projects and proceed with construction using unqualified personnel, undermining safeguards intended to ensure buildings meet approved designs and safety standards. "We have formally written to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, and we hope our request will be considered. Counties must be empowered to take firm action against rogue developers who disregard building regulations and put lives at risk," Sakaja said.

In an advisory issued on October 23, the department said rainfall exceeding 20mm within 24 hours is expected in parts of the Coast, Northeastern region, the Highlands West and East of the Rift Valley, Central Highlands and Southeastern Lowlands from October 24 to 28. The department warned residents to remain alert for flash floods and poor visibility, noting that floodwaters can also occur downstream in areas that have not received heavy rainfall. Platinum group metals, gold, nickel, copper, lithium and rare earth elements lie together in one mineral province in Kaduna State, which the Minister of Solid Minerals Development announced in June as world-class and the Nigerian Geological Survey Agency has verified. The Ministry opens its doors to global investors at Nigeria NOW!, held at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre in Abuja on 19 and 20 November. Processing is following the discoveries, as lithium facilities of $600m in Nasarawa State and $200m near Abuja sit alongside a $400m rare earth processing project in Nasarawa, and mining lease applicants must now submit value-addition plans. Annual mining revenue has risen from about N6bn before the current administration to more than N70bn by the end of 2025.

stories.title: Rwanda: Kagame Defends Strict Dress Codes Amid Rwanda's Dressing Controversy
stories.summary: Rwanda: Kagame Defends Strict Dress Codes Amid Rwanda's Dressing Controversy Village Urugwiro/The New Times President Paul Kagame 23 October 2026 Nile Post (Kampala) By Samuel Muhimba Rwandan President Paul Kagame has defended cultural expectations on dressing, arguing that societies have their own standards of acceptable behaviour which should not be abandoned simply because other countries embrace different ways of life. Speaking on Thursday while addressing more than 10,000 young Rwandans at BK Arena in Kigali during the "Meet The President" session, Kagame said dress codes should be understood within the context of the places people visit and the values of the society in which they live. "If you are going to the beach, by the water, where people go to relax, there is a certain way you can dress and behave that may be different from other places. But imagine someone coming here dressed as though they were at the beach. Wouldn't you all turn around and wonder, what happened to this person?" Kagame asked. Photograph: Rebecca Blackwell/AP Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’ The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday. It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, wrote on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.” The minister of health in Guinea-Bissau, Quinhin Nantote, previously denied that the project would move forward. “This is not even remotely true,” Nantote told the Guardian in Portuguese last week. The study was to be funded with $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), along with another $1.6m from private partners like the Bill Ackman-backed Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation. “The solution is clear here: take the money and vaccinate as many kids as you can,” said Paul Offit, a vaccines expert at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, who sharply criticized the proposed study as unethical.

Le gouvernement a appelé "tous les établissements de santé publics et privés du pays à se mettre en état d’alerte maximale". La République démocratique du Congo est en proie depuis le mois de mai à la 17 e épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola de son histoire, devenue en quelques mois la plus meurtrière jamais connue dans ce vaste pays d' Afrique centrale.

stories.title: RFK Jr’s ‘deities of vaccine research’ raided by police in Guinea-Bissau

Photograph: Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA RFK Jr’s ‘deities of vaccine research’ raided by police in Guinea-Bissau Police seize doses of hepatitis B vaccine from people at center of dispute over research on African newborns Controversial vaccine researchers who have been praised by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) secretary, had their offices in Guinea-Bissau raided by judicial police, who seized doses of hepatitis B vaccines, officials said on Facebook. The researchers have been at the heart of an ongoing dispute over research on African newborns, supported by $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and matched by the Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation for a total of $3.2m. The police search took place on Monday, involving “investigative procedures aimed at clarifying the circumstances related to the said batch of vaccines”, according to the social media post, which was translated from Portuguese.

stories.title: 'Tinubu Must Go!': Nigeria's northern protests test limits of political dissent
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5OTCD Police said the men were found in possession of 'dried leaves,' a pair of scissors and T-shirts bearing the phrase 'Tinubu Must Go!' Image: Borno State Police Command Advertisement T-shirts bearing the slogan "Tinubu Must Go!" — a reference to Nigerian President Bola Tinubu — are at the center of an escalating crackdown on dissent in Nigeria 's vast north. In September, police in the northeastern state of Borno arrested five men, aged between 21 and 44, over the shirts. Authorities have alleged the group had conspired to produce and wear them with the intention of breaching public peace. The men were subsequently charged with criminal conspiracy, inciting disturbance, disturbance of public peace and thuggery. Drawing criticism from human rights groups and activists, police later explained that the arrests followed a routine patrol and that officers had found substances believed to be illicit drugs and other items on the men, arguing that they were not being prosecuted for expressing their political views.

stories.title: Fleeing the frontline: Yemeni families cross Red Sea to Djibouti as Houthi conflict rages
stories.summary: Madinah Abdullah (in pink) and her family members at the Markazi humanitarian site in Obock, Djibouti, on 6 October. Photograph: Carlos Mureithi/The Guardian Their overland routes to safety blocked off, several thousand people have boarded boats to escape gunfire, bombing and a dire humanitarian situation By Carlos Mureithi in Obock A bubaker Saeed was fishing in the Red Sea off Yemen’s coast last month when he noticed explosions in the distance. His mind turned immediately to his wife and two children, and he raced back to his home village of al-Wahijah. Aircraft from the Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemeni government forces had launched airstrikes in surrounding areas, targeting members of the Iran-aligned Houthi militia as its fighters approached the nearby port city of Mocha. “They were bombing Houthis while Houthis were 1km away from us,” the 50-year-old recalled. By the time he reached the shore, the rebels had arrived and were battling government forces on the ground.

stories.title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists
stories.summary: Image source, Reuters Image caption, El Mansouri (left) was named by King Mohammed VI (right) as the country's first female prime minister By Basma El Atti Published 20 October 2026 The Islamic saying "a people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never succeed" has resurfaced in Morocco since King Mohammed VI named Fatima Zahra El Mansouri as the country's first female prime minister. Mustafa Ramid, a former justice minister in an Islamist-led government, cited the saying earlier this month, in a lengthy Facebook post questioning whether a woman should hold the country's highest political office. He argued that Morocco, a Muslim majority country, had found a balance between equality and the responsibilities of state leadership, as the highest office - that of the king - continued to be reserved for men. Morocco operates as a constitutional monarchy. Yet executive power remains in the hands of the 63-year-old monarch.

Photograph: EPA Kenyan starvation cult leader guilty of murder of 190 children and one adult Paul Mackenzie and his church set up sect that ordered followers to starve themselves and their children, say prosecutors A Kenyan court has found the starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and about 30 others guilty of murder over the deaths of ⁠190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult-related disasters in recent history. Mackenzie was arrested in 2023 after police received a tipoff, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest near the coast ⁠in south-eastern Kenya. Prosecutors say Mackenzie and ⁠his Good News International Church organised ​a Christian doomsday sect in which they ordered followers to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended.
